items.title: 18.10.1 Reaction of Acidified Manganate(VII) Ions with Ethanedioate Ions

source_refs.note: Topic 18.10.1 (PDF 33). The printed overall equation (8H+, 5Mn2+, 2CO2) and multipliers are corrected; the printed E of +0.49 V for CO2/C2O4 2- is kept and the usual -0.49 V noted. Flagged for review.

blocks.text: For the reaction between acidified manganate(VII) ions and ethanedioate (oxalate) ions, compare the two reduction half-reactions:

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints E = +0.49 V for 2CO2 + 2e- -> C2O4 2-. Standard tables give about -0.49 V for this couple: carbon dioxide is not an oxidising agent.

The half-reaction with the more positive E proceeds as a reduction, so MnO4- is reduced to Mn2+ (the oxidising agent) and C2O4 2- is oxidised to CO2 (the reducing agent). The number of electrons lost must be equal to number of electrons gained. It is done by multiplying the two half reactions with different coefficients. Here, oxidation half equation is multiplied by 2 and reduction half equation by 5.
book_errors: oxidation half equation is multiplied by 2 and reduction half equation by 5

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The multipliers are the wrong way round: the reduction half-equation (MnO4-, 5 electrons) is multiplied by 2 and the oxidation half-equation (C2O4 2-, 2 electrons) by 5, so that 10 electrons are transferred, as the working below shows.

items: 5 x [C2O4 2- -> 2CO2 + 2e-] (The reaction and E value written in opposite way), E = -0.49 V
The large positive net E value (+1.03 V) indicates that the forward reaction is feasible.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Correct working: with E about -0.49 V for 2CO2 + 2e- -> C2O4 2-, the reversed (oxidation) half-equation has E = +0.49 V. The balanced overall equation is 2MnO4- + 16H+ + 5C2O4 2- -> 2Mn2+ + 10CO2 + 8H2O, and E cell = 1.52 - (-0.49) = +2.01 V. The reaction is feasible, as the book concludes.
